messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for tenant=SableCorp reserved-pool: high_p95_latency (alert id PD-9921). Rule: reserved-pool.latency.p95 > 1200ms for 5m. Link: <https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/PD-9921|view alert>
pd-bot: PD incident PD-9921 created, urgency=high, escalation policy "eng-oncall". Page sent to @oncall.
maya: acked PD-9921 — taking ownership. Seeing spikes in p95 from 600ms -> 1800ms.
alejandro: grabbing slack. What region/cluster?
maya: cluster: dedicated-eu-west-3, pool: sable-reserved-3, affected model variants: rwd-7b and rwd-7b-quant. Impact: ~42% of SableCorp requests hitting degraded latency, tail beyond SLA.
lina: checking pool utilization, evictions, and KV cache pressure. Running quick query.
jonah: p95 correlates with increased batch sizes + KV cache misses after a deploy 30m ago? any rollouts?
maya: no managed rollout flagged but there was an autoscaler config bump at 2578909500 per deploy-bot.
ev an: (typo) eva n -> evan: I'll pull scheduler logs and GPU throttling stats.
lina: quick dump: pool utilization 98%, io-wait and device-queue depth high. KV cache evictions spiked at 2578910500.
maya: mitigation plan: 1) enable fallback routing for SableCorp to their fallback model variant (rwd-7b-small) 2) attempt temporary burst scale +2 GPUs to the reserved pool 3) throttle non-Sable traffic on same pool if feasible.
alejandro: +1 to fallback routing first — lower risk and immediate. Lina, can you flip routing rule?
lina: doing it now — hit command: ```rkctl routing update --tenant sable --from rwd-7b --to rwd-7b-small --percent 100 --reason "auto-fallback due to p95"```
lina: routing update applied. Monitoring effect.
maya: Sable reports initial drop in error rate but latency still high for a subset.
ej: (bot) deploy-bot: autoscaler config update detected at 2578909500 by infra-release.
j onah: meanwhile I'll try a burst scale: ```rkctl pool scale --pool sable-reserved-3 --delta 2 --type gpu```
jonah: scale request accepted, provisioning GPUs — ETA ~3m.
ev an: watching device-level metrics: nvlink errors low, but kernel scheduling queues climbing. Might be a runtime kernel scheduler hotspot.
maya: if burst fails, plan B is to offload some non-critical tenants sharing hosts. Who owns host redistribution?
jonah: I can trigger host affinity shuffle, but that risks short-term task churn. Only do if scale doesn't help.
lina: after routing +scale in flight we see p95 dropping from 1800ms -> 950ms for fallback-routed traffic. Overall pool p95 -> 1100ms.
alejandro: good improvement. Keep watch for 10m window.
customer-success: FYI CS notified SableCorp of degraded performance, asking for ETA and workaround. Sable asked for temporary quota increase to fallbacks.
maya: tracking customer-impact: 42% of requests degraded, error rate unchanged, no request failures. SLO breach potential if p95 stays >1000ms for another 10m.
pd-bot: Reminder: PD escalation timer 12m remaining before team lead escalations.
jonah: scale completed — GPUs added. Device queues decreasing. p95 now ~720ms cluster-wide. Good.
maya: moving to stabilization mode. I'll document timeline and open a follow-up ticket.
alejandro: handing off to next oncall — @evan you monitor until 2578919000 and keep PD updated.
ev an: ack — monitoring. I'll keep the PD incident open until 30m stable, then close.
lina: created runbook note: "reserved-pool-fallback-procedure" with commands used and links. <https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/reserved-pool-fallback|runbook>
maya: created incident ticket INC-2026 with summary and mitigation steps + links to logs.
maya: postmortem action items: - tighten autoscaler rollout checks - add KV cache eviction alert earlier - add safer fallback routing automation for tenancy spikes
j onah: thumbs up.
incident-bot: PD incident PD-9921 status: acknowledged by maya; escalations suspended.
ev an: closing comments: will monitor for 30m, then transition to post-incident review. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
